newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian's lawyer announces death of two women.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian's lawyer announces death of two women.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian's attorney said Wednesday two multiple sclerosis victims had died in the Detroit area in the last 24 hours, but he refused to say whether the assisted suicide advocate was involved.

Lawyer Geoffrey Fieger spoke at a hastily called news conference at which Kevorkian was also present, although he did not answer questions. Fieger said Dorinda Scheipsmeirer, 51, of Oceanside, California, and Lynne Lennox, 54, of Lakewood, New Jersey, were both last seen alive in Michigan.

Police later reported the bodies of two women were found in local hotel rooms. The deaths come less than a week after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled there is no constitutional right to assisted suicide and states have the right to outlaw it.
On June 26, the same day as the ruling, police discovered the body of a Henderson, Nevada, woman in a Detroit-area hotel room. Fieger said he had been retained by the woman's family.
On Wednesday, Fieger said multiple sclerosis had severely limited both women. Scheipsmeirer was a quadriplegic and Lennox had some use of one arm.

Also on Wednesday, Kevorkian, a 69-year-old retired pathologist, called for a panel of non-medical people to draw up guidelines on assisted suicide because the medical profession has refused to endorse the practice.

He has publicly admitted being present at 45 deaths since 1990 and in February Fieger hinted he was involved in two others. Including the two Wednesday, a total of eight more bodies have been found in local hotel rooms since March with notes referring authorities to Fieger's office.
